page: Microsoft Azure F16as_v6 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Fasv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage, requiring external storage solutions, though it is Premium Storage capable. There are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core and text processing capabilities. The single-core stress-ng performance score of 3080.17 and Geekbench single-core score of 2086.0 both rank in the top 25%. Text processing performance is particularly notable, with a Geekbench text processing score of 2742.0 placing it in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 49271.29 and a Passmark CPU score of 36798.15 falling within the middle 50%. Memory performance is solid, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25%, while uncached memory read and write bandwidths remain average at 75.97 GB/sec and 56.09 GB/sec respectively.

For specialized workloads, the F16as_v6 demonstrates top-tier performance in small-model language processing, achieving 349.71 tokens/sec for text generation with a 135M parameter model. However, performance scales down to average levels for medium and large models, such as 17.32 tokens/sec for text generation on a 7B model. The absence of local storage and GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy data-science training or high-I/O database tasks, but its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high clock speed make it a cost-efficient option for general-purpose computing, text processing, web serving, and lightweight inference tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F16as_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the Fasv6 family, powered by a 16-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, 64.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core), and lacks local storage, though it supports Premium Storage. The instance delivers strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores in the top 25%, and top-tier text processing capabilities in the top 10%. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall within average ranges. Lacking a GPU and local storage, this instance is best suited for workloads such as text processing, web serving, and small-scale language model inference where dedicated CPU resources and a balanced 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio provide qualitative resource efficiency.
